newsitem.title: USA: Authority okays two Okla. issues totaling $318 mln.
newsitem.headline: Authority okays two Okla. issues totaling $318 mln.

text.p: Oklahoma Capitol Improvement Authority gave the green light Wednesday for a $300 million road bond offering and an $18 million corrections department bond deal, State Bond Advisor James Joseph said.

"The authorization was given this morning by the Capitol Improvement Authority staff to have them circulate requests for proposals for underwriter, bond counsel and other service providers to get those projects underway," Joseph said.

The authority will issue the $300 million lease revenue road improvement bonds, to be backed by state appropriations, he said. The project will be managed by Oklahoma Department of Transportation pursuant to a contract between Oklahoma DOT and Capitol Improvement Authority.
Plans call for the Oklahoma legislature to appropriate funds to the DOT each year, Joseph said. The DOT will in turn pay the authority, which will then pay bond holders.
Proceeds from the $18 millon corrections bond sale will go mainly to construct three, 200-bed medium-security housing units located at separate sites, Joseph said.
